title: Exactly-Once Semantics
description: Explore exactly-once delivery semantics, the guarantees they provide, and the trade-offs involved in achieving them.

data.text: Exactly-once semantics (EOS) promise that every message is delivered and processed once and only once, regardless of failures. In practice, true exactly-once is extraordinarily difficult because it requires coordination between the broker, the consumer, and any downstream systems. Most systems settle for effectively exactly-once through idempotency combined with careful protocol design.

rows: Message may be lost but never duplicated
Message never lost but may be duplicated

data.text: To deliver exactly once, the broker must not lose the message, the consumer must not process it twice, and any downstream effects must not be applied twice. A single transaction across the broker and database is impossible in most architectures because they are separate systems. Kafka solves this with a two-phase commit protocol that spans the consumer offset and the producer transaction.

data.caption: Two-phase commit flow for exactly-once in Kafka
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Producer
    participant K as Kafka Broker
    participant C as Consumer
    participant D as Database
    P->>K: 1. Begin Transaction
    P->>K: 2. Send Messages
    P->>K: 3. Commit Transaction
    K-->>P: Ack
    C->>K: 4. Fetch with read_committed
    C->>D: 5. Begin Transaction
    C->>D: 6. Process + Write Results
    C->>D: 7. Commit Transaction
    C->>K: 8. Commit Offset in Transaction

data.text: Kafka's transactional producer and consumer APIs are the most mature implementation of exactly-once semantics in a message broker. The producer writes to a transaction, the consumer reads only committed transactions, and both sides coordinate through the transaction coordinator in the broker.

data.title: Node.js — Kafka exactly-once producer
data.content: Use the KafkaJS transactional API for atomic writes.

data.text: RabbitMQ does not support cross-system transactions. Instead, it offers publisher confirms combined with consumer acknowledgements. This gives you at-least-once delivery but requires idempotent consumers to reach effectively exactly-once behavior.

data.title: C# — RabbitMQ with confirms and manual ack
data.content: Combine publisher confirms with manual acknowledgements for maximum reliability.

cards.title: At-most-once
cards.description: Send and forget. No retries, no acks.
cons: Messages can be lost on failure
Unacceptable for financial or critical workflows

cards.title: At-least-once
cards.description: Retry on failure with redelivery. Requires idempotent consumers.

cards.title: Effectively Exactly-once
cards.description: At-least-once delivery plus idempotent processing and transactional persistence.

items.question: Is Kafka the only broker with exactly-once?
items.answer: Kafka is the most mature, but Redpanda and Pulsar also implement transactional APIs. RabbitMQ and SQS do not provide native exactly-once semantics — they require idempotency on the consumer side.

items.question: What does effectively exactly-once mean?
items.answer: It means the system behaves as if it delivers exactly once, but the mechanism is at-least-once delivery combined with idempotent consumers. From the outside, the outcome is identical.

items.question: Should I use transactions for every message?
items.answer: Transactions add latency and complexity. Use them for financial, inventory, or compliance-critical flows. For analytics or event logging, at-least-once with idempotent consumers is usually sufficient.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Exactly-once is a spectrum, not a binary property
At-least-once is the common denominator across all brokers
Kafka transactional API provides the strongest guarantees
data.takeaway: Choose your delivery guarantee based on the cost of duplicates. For most systems, idempotent consumers are the practical path to exactly-once behavior.
